clue.text: Change round elements of shelving for medical history

indicators.note: the two component words of the shelving unit swap places, front part moving to the back

parts.note: a bookcase is a piece of shelving

explanation.surface: Someone rearranges the parts of a shelf unit in order to store patient histories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change round elements of' swaps the two halves of BOOKCASE, putting CASE before BOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's casebook is the written record of patients' cases, a medical history.

clue.text: Found club is too hard to work with

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A newly formed club proves too difficult to cooperate with.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast iron is brittle and unyielding, so the phrase describes something too rigid to be worked.

clue.text: Scorn food

definitions.meaning: slang for grub, something to eat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to jeer at contemptuously and, informally, to eat greedily or a meal itself.

clue.text: Price reductions here preclude profit headquarters intended to announce

parts.note: to bar something is to preclude it
gain is a synonym of profit

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so the words are taken as spoken

parts.note: headquarters is a base, intended is meant

explanation.surface: An instruction to block profits that headquarters planned to declare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to announce' applies only to BASE MEANT, which spoken sounds like BASEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A store's bargain basement is the floor where cut-price goods are sold.

clue.text: Bit 'of flag-waving for this bad team?

definitions.text: Bit 'of flag-waving for this bad team?

parts.words: Bit 'of flag-waving for this bad team
parts.note: a football linesman raises his flag for this infringement, and read as two words it suggests a team playing poorly

explanation.surface: A side playing badly prompts some flag-waving from the officials.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby the assistant referee waves a flag when a player is caught in an illegal forward position; 'bad team' splits the answer into 'off' (poor) and 'side' (team).
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught ahead of play illegally is the infringement signalled by the linesman's raised flag.

clue.text: Sort of wedding that wasted time for military dictator

indicators.note: something wasted is lost, so a letter disappears from the wedding word

parts.note: a shotgun wedding is a hurried one forced by pregnancy

explanation.surface: A rushed marriage that lost time somehow linked to a warlord.
explanation.definitionFit: The shogun was the hereditary military ruler of feudal Japan, a dictator in all but name.

clue.text: Remarkable offering used to bring the past alive

definitions.text: used to bring the past alive

parts.note: historic means notable or momentous
a present is a gift or offering

explanation.surface: A notable gift serves to make history vivid.
explanation.definitionFit: This grammatical tense narrates past events in present-tense verbs to make them vivid.

clue.text: Watched over empty lorry with caution

parts.note: to guard is to watch over

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its inside, keeping only first and last letters

explanation.surface: An empty truck was kept under careful watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting guardedly means behaving warily and cautiously.

clue.text: Poles keep only fashionable garments

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the poles enclose the rest

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles

indicators.note: read as 'able to be fashioned', the word is reshaped

explanation.surface: People from Poland retain only clothes that are in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' misleads toward people from Poland; here it is the north and south poles, and 'fashionable' works as 'able to be fashioned', so the word 'only' is remade inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Biting insect disappears in ditch

indicators.note: the insect vanishes, so its letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: trenchant means incisive or biting
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A stinging bug vanishes into a gully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappears' takes ANT off TRENCHANT; 'Biting' looks like a description of the insect but is an adjective for sharp words.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow channel dug in the ground, a ditch.

clue.text: Sulphur has disagreeable scent

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
poor in the sense of bad or unsatisfactory

explanation.surface: Sulphur gives off an unpleasant smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or trail, including the scent, left by a wild animal.

clue.text: Block after warning shout to play for time

parts.note: golfers cry fore to warn those ahead of a ball
to stall is to delay deliberately

explanation.surface: A golfer obstructs play after crying a warning, trying to waste time.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent or thwart something by acting first.

clue.text: Blowing up into final shape

indicators.note: to shape letters is to mould them into a new form

explanation.surface: Puffing something up until it reaches its finished form.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is the act of filling with air, blowing up a balloon or tyre.

clue.text: Under an obligation not to live hard long ago

indicators.note: the word signals that the following pieces are absent from the longer word

parts.note: beholden means owing a debt or obligation
to be is to exist or live
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone indebted, unable to live a tough life, in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes BE and H from the front of BEHOLDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an archaic adjective for bygone, of a time long past.

clue.text: Fault to do with the receiver

parts.note: of can mean concerning or relating to
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A mistake connected with the telephone handset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' suggests a telephone, but it is the criminal sense: someone who handles stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a wrongdoing or transgression, a fault.

clue.text: Paying nothing for meals in upper part of ship

parts.note: free means costing nothing
board is meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Free meals offered on the top deck of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeboard is the part of a ship's side above the waterline, its upper section.

clue.text: Styling of musical function

parts.note: Hair is a famous 1960s rock musical
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: The style of a show's party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a styled arrangement of the hair.

clue.text: The fan is sticking

definitions.meaning: clinging or adhering to a surface

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a supporter; as an adjective it means clinging or stuck fast.

clue.text: Take oneself off for an overhaul

definitions.meaning: to go somewhere, as in withdrawing to another room

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to betake oneself to a place and a fix or renovation.

clue.text: Masseur finds what tourist has in neck?

definitions.meaning: a gawping sightseer is a rubberneck, so this is the word placed before neck

explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is one who massages, and also the first half of rubberneck, a gawping tourist.

clue.text: Staring in astonishment, like a sailorman?

definitions.meaning: the cartoon sailor Popeye, so resembling him

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means wide-eyed with surprise, and split it suggests the spinach-eating sailor of cartoons.

clue.text: American friend taking nothing from indulgent vendor

indicators.note: taking one piece from another means removing it
names the word that loses the letter

parts.note: a medieval pardoner sold indulgences
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Yankee mate pockets nothing from a generous seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... from' removes O from PARDONER; 'indulgent' means selling indulgences, not lenient.
explanation.definitionFit: Pardner is a folksy American variant of partner, used for a friend or buddy.

clue.text: Prison may offer a series of steps for girls

definitions.text: a series of steps for girls

parts.note: the can is slang for jail
can means is able or permitted, like may

explanation.surface: A jail might provide a staircase for young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps' suggests stairs, but these are dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking dance performed by a line of female dancers.

clue.text: Execute bet — go easy!

indicators.note: executing by beheading takes the head, the first letter, off

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

explanation.surface: Place your wager and take it easy!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' beheads GAMBLE, losing its first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow relaxed pace.

clue.text: Comic imitation of American striptease

definitions.meaning: in the US, a variety show featuring striptease

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mocking parody and an American variety show with strip acts.

clue.text: One who states the price, say, for a share

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be heard rather than seen

parts.note: a quoter gives a quotation or price

explanation.surface: Someone naming the price for a stake.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech QUOTER and QUOTA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A quota is an allotted portion or share.

clue.text: Lizard made way round hot Spanish city

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the next, enclosing it

parts.note: came means moved towards, made one's way
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
Leon is a city in northern Spain

explanation.surface: A lizard travelled around a hot city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts H inside CAME, giving CHAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a colour-changing lizard.

clue.text: Summon girl without approval

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the girl surrounds the approval

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
OK means approval

explanation.surface: Call up a girl who has no permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up or summon a feeling or memory.

clue.text: We're told it's fresh air, so undress

indicators.note: a hint that the phrase is heard aloud

parts.note: fresh is new, an air is a tune or ditty

explanation.surface: Someone claims stripping off is good for getting fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' is a song, not the atmosphere: NEW DITTY sounds like NUDITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Undress as a noun means the state of being unclothed, nakedness.

clue.text: Publicist has pamphlet to keep going

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: A press agent holds a leaflet to keep things running.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or extend, keeping something going.
